2. Heard Sri Santosh Shukla, learned counsel for the revisionist, Sri Jitendra Singh, learned Brief Holder for the State of U.P. and perused the records.
3.

The present revision under Sections 397/401 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the revisionist Narendra Kumar against the judgement and order dated 11.2.2009 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Auraiya in Criminal Appeal No. 2 of 2005 by which the said appeal has been dismissed and the judgement and order dated 3.2.2005 passed by the trial court has been affirmed, and, further against the judgement and order dated 3.2.2005 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate, Auraiya in Case No. 676 of 2000, under Section 7/16 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, whereby the revisionist has been sentenced for 06 months simple imprisonment and a fine of Rs.1000/- and in default of payment of fine to further additional simple imprisonment of 01 month by recording conviction under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

sentences.text: The facts of the case are that on 30.12.1998 at about 01.00 pm the revisionist was found selling and demonstrating pulses along with other articles in his shop situated at Erwa Katra by the complainant N.R. Pandey, Food Inspector.

On suspicion of it being adulterated, he disclosed his identity to the accused and purchased 750 gm gram pulse (chana daal) for sample from the accused by giving Rs.15/- and gave notice and took signature of the accused on it.
After preparation of sample in three polythene bag in equal part sent to the public analyst for analysis.
The public analyst found the sample to be adulterated as 1.10 per cent khesari daal was found in it.
The complainant then took sanction from the C.M.O. concerned and filed a complaint against the revisionist/accused.

In the trial court the complainant/Ram N.R. Pandey was examined as P.W.-1, Kush Kumar Gupta,
the clerk was examined as P.W.-2.
The accused/revisionist in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case and stated of false implication.
No defense evidence was led.
The trial court convicted and sentenced the accused/revisionist as stated above.
The appeal was preferred against the same which came to be dismissed after which the present revision has been filed against both the impugned judgement and orders.

5. Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that there has been inordinate delay in filing of the complaint inasmuch as the sample of the alleged food article was taken on 30.12.1998 which was sent for testing to the public analyst after which the public analyst gave its report dated 18.1.1999 but the present complaint of the case has been filed on 09.3.2000.
It is submitted that subsequently notice was sent by P.W.-2 along with public analyst report through registered post as alleged on 01.4.2000.
It is submitted that there has been inordinate delay of about 01 year and 02 months in filing of the complaint.
It is submitted that the delay in filing of the complaint is not explained at all and is enormous.
It is submitted that sending of the notice under Section 13(2) of the Act along with the report of public analyst to the revisionist was after about 22 days of the filing of the complaint.

It is submitted that looking to the facts that the complaint has been filed after about 01 year and 2 months of the date of report of public analyst for which there is no plausible explanation given and then the said report being sent to the revisionist with notice under Section 13(2) of the Act even 22 days thereafter, clearly deprives the revisionist of exercising his valuable right under Section 13(2) of the Act.
It is submitted that looking to the same, the revision be allowed and the judgement and order of the trial court along with the judgement and order of the appellate court be set aside.

6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. opposed the revision and submitted that there is no illegality,
irregularity or infirmity in the impugned judgements and orders of the trial court court as well as the appellate court.

7. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the complaint has been filed after about 01 year and 02 moths of the date of report of public analyst.
The delay in launching of the prosecution is clearly unexplained.

Notice under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is said to have been sent along with the report of public analyst after 22 days of the filing of the complaint to the revisionist by registered post.
The right of the revisionist in getting his sample re-tested by the Central Food Laboratory expeditiously gets defeated.
The delay in filing of the complaint is totally unexplained.

sentences.text: The present revision is allowed.

The impugned judgement and order dated 11.2.2009 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Auraiya in Criminal Appeal No. 2 of 2005 and the judgement and order dated 3.2.2005 passed by Chief Judicial Magistrate, Auraiya in Case No. 676 of 2000, under Section 7/16 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 are hereby set aside.
9. The revisionist- Narendra Kumar is acquitted of the charge levelled against him.
The revisionist is on bail.

His bail bond is cancelled and sureties discharged.
10.
Office is directed to transmit the copy of this judgement along with the trial court records to the concerned trial court forthwith for its compliance and necessary action.
11. The file be consigned to records.
(Samit Gopal,J.) Order Date :- 20.3.2024/
